answer: Give every newcomer a sparrow-sized stake in a mutual-insurance circle of strangers, not a private badge. Each circle co-insures small deals: if one member cheats, the whole circle pays, so members vet each other hard. Standing grows only as the circle survives random gale stress-tests, where auditors plant a fake deal and watch who catches it, and a comet-trail record shows every payout and rescue in public. A farm's fakes insure only each other, so one fraud drains its whole circle at once, while honest circles deepen through shared risk, not headcount.
